findings.evidence: Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Simple.lean:54-55 defines `Simple.mono_isIso_iff_nonzero`; the weaker zero-or-isomorphism claim is also satisfied by the zero object.
findings.fix: State the actual condition: for every monomorphism `f` into `X`, `IsIso f ↔ f ≠ 0` (equivalently, include the required nonzero-object condition).
findings.issue: The module docstring says `CategoryTheory.Simple X` merely means every monomorphism into `X` is zero or an isomorphism, omitting the condition excluding the zero object.

findings.evidence: AsModule.lean:113 says “Neither direction is new work: forwards…”; Symmetric/Specht/Completeness.lean:166 identifies the uniqueness proof lemma, and lines 205-208 enumerate the injectivity and surjectivity proofs.
findings.fix: Remove the implementation paragraphs and retain concise descriptions of the results and their consumer-facing meaning.
findings.issue: The public `nonempty_fdRepIso_iff` docstring narrates both proof directions instead of documenting only the interface; similar proof narration appears on `existsUnique_nonempty_linearEquiv_spechtModule` and `spechtModuleFDRepClass_bijective`.

summary: The new documentation inaccurately characterizes categorical simplicity and includes implementation-focused material in public theorem docstrings.
